article_title: AWS Renames Amazon Q Developer's Console Tool 'AWS Assistant' and Starts Retiring Its GitHub App Ahead of 2027 Kiro Deadlines

content_preview.title: AWS Renames Amazon Q Developer's Console Tool 'AWS Assistant' and Starts Retiring Its GitHub App Ahead of 2027 Kiro Deadlines
content_preview.summary: AWS renamed Amazon Q Developer's console assistant to 'AWS assistant' on November 5 and is cutting off new GitHub App installs, two more steps in its year-long wind-down of Q Developer toward Kiro.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

AWS has renamed the version of Amazon Q Developer built into the AWS Management Console to "AWS assistant," according to an [AWS "What's New" post](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/q-developer-renamed-aws-assistant/) dated Nov 5, 2026. Days later, the company began shutting off new installs of the separate Amazon Q Developer GitHub App, according to a [notice on the app's GitHub listing](https://github.com/apps/amazon-q-developer). Both moves are part of a wind-dow...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article (759 words, within the 400-1200 range). Five clearly headed sections (Overview, What Changed in the Console, The GitHub App Is Being Retired Separately, Context: A Year-Long Wind-Down Toward Kiro, What We Don't Know). The 'Context' section does useful synthesis — connecting the Nov 5 console rename to the list of surfaces the April 2026 end-of-support post explicitly exempted from the Kiro sunset — without overstating what the sources say. The closing 'What We Don't Know' section is an honest, explicit absence disclosure rather than a filled-in guess.
